title: Artificial turf puddling? Check the base

C.name: IMG_6074.jpg
C.note: the file has 6 black rows at its bottom edge; pos 50% 0% keeps them out of the band

headline: TURF *PUDDLING?*
CHECK THE *BASE*
beats.vo: Puddles on your artificial turf? Turf drains through its base, so that's where to look.

headline: *COMPACTED*
GRAVEL BASE
beats.vo: Dig out four to six inches, lay a *weed barrier,* then three to four inches of *compacted crushed gravel.*

headline: SLOPED AWAY.
*EDGES NAILED*
beats.vo: The base *slopes away* from the house, and the edges get *nailed down* tight.

headline: STILL NEEDS
*SOME CARE*
beats.vo: It's *low maintenance,* not no maintenance. Blow the *leaves off* this fall. Wet leaves hold moisture and feed *moss.*

post.caption: Puddles on artificial turf in the Lower Mainland usually point to the base. A typical install uses a weed barrier and 3-4 inches of compacted crushed gravel (wet clay may need more, or a drain), sloped away from the house, and never plastic underneath. In leaf season, blow the leaves off before they hold moisture and feed moss.
post.alt: A long artificial turf backyard beside a concrete walkway and cedar fence, an animated diagram of the gravel base layers under the turf, a crisp turf edge against a concrete pad, and artificial turf in front of a framed cedar fence.
